title: Regent Moray to John Wood, Edinburgh, 13 July 1568 (BL Add MS 32091 f. 213)

plaintext.source: Not in Bain's Calendar of Scottish Papers ii; no clear text online.

transcription.notes: Semicolon-separated file the measure tool does not split; counts from NOTES. BL viewer offline, so symbol identities are unchecked. 14 Nov 2026: the contributor of issue #553 re-transcribed from the DECODE R8345 image (aaymeloglu/transcription.txt), splitting five of Tomokiyo's symbols; the order and length agree with Tomokiyo's.

system.summary: 32 symbols (x and z families with variants, numbers 10-19, letters) with repeats suggesting a homophonic alphabet; not read, word codes possible.
system.sibling_key: The Queins Cipher (HMC 6th Report) and the 1569-71 Scottish keys checked; none matches the symbol set.
system.notes: IC 0.0496; 9 hapax. No single symbol behaves as a null or separator.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: obtained a DECODE login with privileges and passed its session cookie (from the browser developer tools) to the model, set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5, and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
tools: Scots quadgram and 5-gram models (lm.py, qg.py, ng5.py)

solution.what: Catalogue of Additions, Bain ii, HMC 6th Report and DECODE searched; letter not in print.
Counts, IC, repeats; 'r 17 10' = the tried and not preferred.
5-gram Scots annealer reads 5 of 6 matched 134-letter controls.
Homophonic annealing under Scots, English, French and Latin models.
Nulls, separators and merged variant families tested.
Rare symbols as word codes; matched control shows the test has no power.
Twenty words and names dragged over 730 placements; none supported.

Issue #553 (aaymeloglu) integrated: own decoder aaymeloglu/own_decode.py reproduces reading.txt; the 134-glyph sequence matches Tomokiyo's position by position apart from five splits; splits not checked on the R8345 image (private, no login); strict count 27/35 words = 77%.

outcome.method_basis: By the contributor (GitHub issue #553, aaymeloglu): a new glyph transcription from the DECODE R8345 image that splits five of Tomokiyo's symbols, then annealing over glyph-to-letter maps scored by Scots dictionary segmentation, with values held from a first run (sending, freindis, oure). The project's own attempt of Sept 2026 on Tomokiyo's transcription failed: Homophonic annealing under Scots, English, French and Latin models, null and word-code hypotheses and crib dragging on Tomokiyo's transcription gave no reading; matched controls were read.
outcome.fraction_read_source: aaymeloglu/reading.md: words of the Scots reading, 27 of 35 read under the strict rule (holes: [Q], [Q2], [and], Carlyle, la??is, spil, e?, the last word), counted 14 Nov 2026
outcome.notes: Reading by the contributor; transcription splits not checked on the image here (R8345 private, no login in the integration session). The project's own Sept 2026 attempt on Tomokiyo's transcription failed because his symbol 19 carries both 'the' and 'm'.

gaps.detail: check on the DECODE R8345 image with a login

gaps.detail: one or two occurrences each in 134 glyphs
read as the Queen by sense only

texts.label: Cipher postscript, f. 213v
texts.summary: Moray tells Wood that letting Mary remain at Carlisle and sending Lord Fleming home has done great harm, and that if she comes home it will ruin the whole, as far as the reading goes; the last word is unresolved.

credits.note: transcription of the Moray-Wood cipher (cryptiana elizabeth.htm), the only ciphertext available
